onboarding.title: Screenpunk MCP
onboarding.body:
Screenpunk starts its local controller and hidden preview helper automatically when this MCP server launches. The Mac workbench does not need to be visibly open.

Preview is live by default. Actions in a live preview can control approved devices. Screenshot capture itself does not click controls.

Deployment of a previewed revision is agent-mediated chat approval, not a cryptographic guarantee.

Device recovery: hold two fingers on the device screen for five seconds to open the device menu, then choose Disconnect and confirm. Only confirming Disconnect erases screens, credentials, and pairing. Forgetting an unreachable device on the Mac does not erase it.

unlink.title: Disconnect a device
unlink.body:
Hold two fingers on the device screen for five seconds to open the device menu, then choose Disconnect and confirm. Opening the menu does not erase anything. Confirming Disconnect erases screens, credentials, and pairing.

Forgetting an unreachable device on the Mac does not erase it. This Mac has forgotten the device. To remove its screens and pairing, hold two fingers on its screen for five seconds to open the device menu, then choose Disconnect and confirm.

Disconnect is confirmed on the device. Forget on the Mac is not remote erasure or upstream-token revocation.

preview.title: Live preview
preview.body:
preview_dashboard returns PNG image content rendered by Screenpunk's hidden helper, plus revision digest, target dimensions, rendering platform, connection health, and diagnostics. It never returns only a local path.

Preview is live by default. Live preview — actions control your devices. Capture does not click controls. Failed renders return render_timeout or SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE without a placeholder image.

A dark dashboard can be legitimate. Failed rendering is detected through readiness, not by rejecting dark pixels.

pairing.title: Pairing
pairing.body:
A device allows one owner. Pairing runs over the TLS 1.3 LAN link with a six-digit SAS matching code and never self-approves through MCP.

1. discover_services lists _screenpunk._tcp advertisements; pass host and port from the device's unpaired screen if Bonjour is blocked.
2. request_pairing returns the matching code. Show it to the user; the device shows its own code.
3. Only if both codes match, the user taps Confirm on the device. Then call confirm_pairing. Until the device owner confirms there, confirm_pairing returns permission_required.

Codes expire after two minutes. A device owned by another Mac returns not_paired (second_owner) until it is unlinked on the device. forget_device removes the device from this Mac only and does not erase the device. New or expanded connections return permission_required until approved in native settings.

deploy.title: Deploy
deploy.body:
deploy_dashboard ships the exact revision the user reviewed: preview_dashboard it first, ask the user in chat, then call deploy_dashboard with that revision and approved=true. Revisions this controller never previewed return permission_required. This is agent-mediated chat approval, not a cryptographic guarantee.

Transfer runs over the paired TLS 1.3 LAN link. The device checks every file hash and the target orientation and size before activating. A failed or interrupted transfer returns phase failed and the device keeps its current dashboard. deploy_dashboard is idempotent on deploymentId; reuse the same id to retry. rollback_dashboard redeploys a revision from the device's history through the same path. Devices fetch their own HTTP and WebSocket data; the Mac is not a runtime proxy.
